excluded_operator_suggestion.text:
The training-free per-sample scale predictor from X (TabPFN in-context
regression, or the kNN degraded form) is excluded from the s5 knob pool for
three reasons, all in `iteration_1.md`:
(1) **Territory** — an auxiliary regressor fitted on the train split and
inserted into the forward path is a second predictor composed with the network
(APEX's construction, which the websearcher found the literature frames as
architecture); the verdict's zero-parameter clause covers statistics of the
sample's own inference-available data, not the fitting algorithm of an auxiliary
model, and TabPFN would import a pretrained transformer's learned weights.
s6/s4 territory, and 12.5's "no new paradigms" independently excludes it.
(2) **Dominated where it matters** — measured leave-one-out kNN-in-X on
`ext__helmholtz_2d`: logRMSE 0.875, pred/true p95/p5 = 14.2 (~2.4x typical
multiplicative error) vs **1.74** for the free LF-field statistic (8x looser),
on the one dataset with amplitude headroom.
(3) **No headroom where it is uniquely usable** — `ifc_poisson` is the only
panel dataset where X reaches and LF does not (test ships `fidelity_64` only),
and there the raw per-sample scale spread is 3.2x with B1 turn 2 measuring
alpha ~ 0.996.
**Handed to s6/s4** with those numbers: any APEX-like amplitude-anchor
composition should read the **LF field**, not X; the kNN form needs no new
dependency and can be screened for free.

test_error_concentration_paired.what: per-sample test-error concentration, arm (zscore) vs the paired H100 same-hardware cap-12 seed-0 champion (maxabs). Descriptive aggregations of the rel_l2_per_sample arrays published in the per-dataset training JSONs — NOT a re-scored metric.
test_error_concentration_paired.effective_N_definition: 1 / sum_i s_i^2 with s_i = (rel_l2_i)^2 / sum_j (rel_l2_j)^2 — the participation ratio of the TEST squared-error distribution. This is the test-side analogue of the train-side effective-N statistic the s2-B2 mechanism pass reported; the two are not the same quantity and are not directly comparable.

findings: F1 (turn 1) The pre-registered cross-stream hypothesis -- that zscore repairs the outlier-dominated MF loss (s2_beyond_copy-B2's effective-N mechanism) -- is FALSIFIED for this family. On ext__helmholtz_2d's HF train stage the top-1 sample's share of MSE energy is 0.99284 under maxabs and 0.99117 under zscore; the participation-ratio effective N is 1.0145/400 vs 1.0179/400 (LF stage 3.030 vs 3.032). The reason is arithmetic: a global scalar divides every sample's energy by the same constant, so only the centring term can move relative sample weights, and helmholtz's |mu|/sd is 0.0415. The outlier domination is real and worse than reported on the raw target (per-sample RMS max/median = 1698) -- and it survives the scaler change untouched.

F2 (turn 1) What zscore changed is where the learnable population sits in the network's output range. Typical normalized train target rms(Y)/s: maxabs 0.02536 vs zscore 1.0; max|Y|/rms = 39.44; the maxabs divisor is 7.3826 against a target sd of 0.18704.

F3 (turn 1) 91.6% of helmholtz's log nRMSE gain is per-sample AMPLITUDE calibration. nRMSE 6.4680 -> 1.8998 (ratio 3.405), but after an oracle per-sample rescale the two arms are 0.8166 vs 0.7370 (ratio 1.108). The maxabs model emits 2.039x the HF RMS with alpha_median -0.0209 (its optimal rescale is a ~48x shrink AND a sign flip); the zscore model hedges quiet at 0.377x with alpha_median +0.320.

F4 (turn 1) The helmholtz pattern gain is real but population-wide, not a tail re-fit: corr_demeaned 0.0362 -> 0.4021 (median -0.0041 -> 0.5590), 75/100 samples improved, improved-fraction by target-amplitude quartile 0.60/0.88/0.80/0.72, Spearman(amplitude, gain) = -0.025. Spectrally the arm moved from 'loud garbage' to 'too quiet': predicted/HF energy in the band holding 99.997% of HF energy is 4.168 (maxabs) vs 0.134 (zscore), error/HF energy 4.500 -> 1.100 (1.00 == emitting nothing).

F5 (turn 2) The pre-registered leverage covariate |mu|/sd has ZERO separating power between the two movers and the four nulls (movers 0.0415 and 1.426; worst null 3.749 = fisher_kpp). The scale ratio separates cleanly: G = max|Y_train|/sd(Y_train) gives movers 39.47 and 9.858 vs worst null 5.997 (margin 1.64x), and the tail-only variant max/rms gives 39.44 and 5.660 vs 2.537 (margin 2.23x). Spearman of |delta skill|/min_claimable_effect against max_over_sd is 0.943, against |mu|/sd 0.714, against hf_dc_energy_share 0.257.

F6 (turn 2) The mechanism-correct decomposition: under maxabs the supervised target has pedestal mu/max and fluctuation RMS sd/max; zscore sets these to 0 and 1, so it magnifies the fluctuation by exactly G = max/sd = (max/rms) x (rms/sd) = tail-term x pedestal-term. helmholtz's G is nearly pure tail (39.44 x 1.001), sharp__fisher_kpp_2d's is nearly pure pedestal (1.55 x 3.88 -- exactly why it was mispredicted), ifc_poisson's is mixed (5.66 x 1.74).

F7 (turn 2) G is necessary but not sufficient: sharp__fisher_kpp_2d has the 3rd-largest G (5.997) and a dead pattern channel (corr_demeaned 0.0029 control -> 0.0042 arm) and moved +0.042; sharp__cahn_hilliard has the most learnable pattern on the sharp side (corr 0.733) but the smallest G (1.322) and moved -0.076. Both movers have G >= 9.86 AND a live pattern channel.

F8 (turn 2) Function displacement ||pred_arm - pred_ctrl||/||pred_ctrl|| does not track the score in either direction: helmholtz 0.993 (cosine 0.130 -- a different function), sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d 0.425, sharp__cahn_hilliard 0.244, sharp__fisher_kpp_2d 0.076, ifc_poisson 0.035, sharp__allen_cahn_2d 0.026. The panel's only claimable win came from a 3.5% move of the learned function; the two sharp sets whose functions moved 24-42% scored identically.

F9 (turn 2) ifc_poisson's gain contains NO amplitude/level/pattern-onset component: corr_demeaned 0.99372 -> 0.99393, alpha_median 0.99896 -> 0.99881, pred_rms/target_rms 1.00023 -> 1.00011; amplitude share of the log gain -9.1% (helmholtz +91.6%, the four sharp sets ~0).

F10 (turn 3) ifc_poisson's 23% is a coherent step down the error: cos(displacement, control error) mean 0.605 / median 0.639 against a random baseline of 0.0125, 99.2% of 128 test samples moved toward the truth, displacement 0.753x the control error norm, optimal step along it 0.84.

F11 (turn 3) ifc_poisson moves by the SAME magnification channel, acting on the resolved band. Under maxabs its HF train target sits at pedestal 0.1447 / fluctuation 0.1014 (G = 9.86). Band 0 (k < 7.54) carries 99.88% of HF energy and supplies 98.7% of the removed error energy, cut to 0.605x; bands >= 3 got marginally worse (1.008-1.049). Relative DC error 1.914% -> 1.149%; DC share of squared error 0.1344 -> 0.0811.

F12 (turn 3) The stage-seam explanation for ifc_poisson is REFUTED. Under maxabs its LF and HF stages are placed almost identically (pedestal 0.1556 vs 0.1447; fluctuation-RMS mismatch 1.117), so the pretrain->finetune transfer was not mis-scaled. The panel's largest maxabs stage mismatch is helmholtz at 1.357; no dataset has a stage seam that could explain its movement. (ifc_poisson does fit its HF scaler on only N_hf = 5 fields, but the placement geometry, not estimator noise, is what moved.)

F13 (turn 3) Sharp-2D: the scaler acts, but its entire available effect is an order of magnitude below the round's floor. cos(displacement, control error) / fraction of samples moved toward truth: sharp__allen_cahn_2d -0.013 / 0.46 (a coin-flip re-roll), sharp__fisher_kpp_2d 0.076 / 0.92, sharp__cahn_hilliard 0.295 / 0.82, sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d 0.539 / 0.95 -- yet the nRMSE moves are 0.2635->0.2688, 0.2521->0.2590, 0.4876->0.4784, 0.5134->0.5022, i.e. -2.2% at best against floors worth 10-22% of skill.

F14 (turn 3) The three LEVEL_ONLY sharp sets sit AT their level-only ceiling under both scalers: arm nRMSE / constant-field oracle = 1.037 (allen_cahn), 1.045 (fisher_kpp), 1.439 (pfc), with demeaned correlation 0.012->0.002, 0.003->0.004, 0.011->-0.006. Their score is the DC term, which a linear output bias reproduces for free under any affine target scaler.

F15 (turn 3) The displacement is almost entirely PATTERN everywhere except helmholtz: pattern share 0.963 (allen_cahn), 0.998 (fisher_kpp), 0.991 (pfc), 0.973 (cahn_hilliard), 0.849 (ifc_poisson), 0.399 on ext__helmholtz_2d (60.1% DC). Helmholtz is the only panel dataset where the scaler moved the predicted LEVEL -- the amplitude/level channel s5-B1 named is real and helmholtz-specific.
interpretation: MECHANISM (high confidence; F1-F3, F6 are arithmetic-level and reproduce from the train split alone): in this LF-blind pretrain/finetune FNO family the output-target scaler is a DYNAMIC-RANGE PLACEMENT device, not a sample-weighting device. It has two separable components. The PEDESTAL (mu) is absorbed for free by the output layer's bias -- it changes nothing, which is why the card's |mu|/sd covariate inverted the ordering. The FLUCTUATION MAGNIFICATION G = max|Y_train|/sd(Y_train) is what optimization cannot absorb: under maxabs, max|Y| is set by the single most extreme train field (1698x the median sample on helmholtz), so the whole learnable population is supervised at 2.5% of the network's output range and its residual output error is re-amplified by max|Y| at denormalization.

CORRECTED PREDICTOR (moderate-to-high confidence; n = 6 datasets, single seed, two movers): a global output-target scaler is a lever on dataset D iff (1) G = max|Y_train|/sd(Y_train) is large -- observed break between 6.0 (no effect) and 9.9 (effect) -- AND (2) D's pattern channel is alive, i.e. D is not LEVEL_ONLY under tools/dc_pattern_split.py. Neither factor alone predicts anything on this panel: fisher_kpp has (1) without (2) and cahn_hilliard has (2) without (1), and both are nulls. Use G, not |mu|/sd; report its tail x pedestal decomposition, because a G that is mostly pedestal (fisher_kpp 1.55 x 3.88) is a G that will do nothing.

The two movers spend the same magnification differently, which is the useful part of the result: on a BROKEN predictor (helmholtz, corr 0.036) G buys per-sample amplitude calibration (91.6% of the log gain) and only 1.11x of real field content; on a WORKING predictor (ifc_poisson, corr 0.994) G buys a uniform ~40% cut of the error energy in the band that carries 99.9% of the signal. The panel-level lesson is that normalization repairs CALIBRATION, and calibration is worth a lot of nRMSE precisely where the model was miscalibrated, not where it was uninformed.

SHARP-2D VERDICT (high confidence): the 'normalization explains the sharp-2D DC-predictor collapse' hypothesis is CLOSED, negatively. The three LEVEL_ONLY sets are at 1.04-1.44x their own constant-field oracle with demeaned correlation ~0 under both scalers; their G (1.32-6.00) contains too little magnification to matter; and the two sharp sets whose solutions did move toward the truth (pfc cos 0.539, cahn_hilliard cos 0.295) bought about 2% of nRMSE against floors worth 10-22%. What sharp-2D lacks is a mechanism that produces PATTERN -- LF-conditioned and local, per the s6/s4 locality findings -- not a better target parameterization.

SPECULATIVE (H3, untested here): the family clips gradients at grad_clip = 1.0. Under maxabs the helmholtz loss is ~1/1558 of the zscore loss, so the clip almost certainly never binds, while under zscore the dominant sample's normalized target reaches ~39 and its batches plausibly clip. If so, whatever robustification the outlier-dominated loss received came from the CLIPPER, not from the scaler. Testing this needs training-time instrumentation (gradient-norm and clip-rate logging per batch) and is a B3 item.

SPECULATIVE (H4): pfc and cahn_hilliard displaced their functions by 24-42% at constant score. Consistent with a flat basin whose emitted content is largely orthogonal to the truth, but I have no same-arm different-seed predictions to calibrate a displacement noise floor -- any future card that dumps two seeds' preds_test.npz would close this cheaply.
6_analysis.falsification_postmortem: The clause did not fire because ifc_poisson moved 0.3805 > its 0.240 floor on all three pre-registered bases, and the mechanism behind that single dataset is now identified: it is the SAME output-range magnification G = max|Y|/sd = 9.86 that drove helmholtz (G = 39.47), acting on a model whose pattern channel was already alive (corr 0.994), delivering 98.7% of its removed error energy in the band carrying 99.88% of the signal. The clause's consequent -- 'the amplitude/level channel is confined to ext__helmholtz_2d' -- is therefore false in the right way: the LEVEL channel really is helmholtz-specific (60.1% of the helmholtz displacement is DC, versus 0.2-15% everywhere else, F15), but the SCALER channel is not, because on a working predictor it acts on the pattern instead. The half of the clause that DID hold (leave-helmholtz-out geomean 0.3287 < 0.884) is explained by F13/F14: four of the six panel datasets have G <= 6.0 and/or a dead pattern channel, so there was no panel-level movement available to buy. And the card's own leverage prediction failed for a now-understood reason -- it ranked datasets by the pedestal term |mu|/sd, which a linear output bias makes free, instead of by the fluctuation magnification G. The single most consequential correction is F1: the cross-stream 'effective-N repair' story that motivated the arm is not what happened; effective N is 1.0145 -> 1.0179 out of 400, i.e. unchanged, and the outlier domination still has to be fixed in the objective.
surprises: The effective N of the training loss is IDENTICAL under the two scalers (1.0145 vs 1.0179 of 400 on helmholtz). The mechanism the arm was designed around cannot be moved by any global scalar -- and nobody had checked, in either stream, that the two normalizations imply different sample weights. They do not.

The panel's only claimable win (ifc_poisson) came from a 3.5% displacement of the learned function, while sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d's function moved 42.5% -- and toward the truth (cos 0.539) -- for a 2.2% nRMSE change that is 4.6x inside its floor. Score movement and function movement are nearly uncorrelated on this panel.

91.6% of the big helmholtz 'pattern recovery' is per-sample amplitude calibration; after an oracle rescale the two arms differ by only 1.108x. The headline -70.6% is mostly the maxabs model being 2.04x too loud and sign-inverted (alpha_median -0.0209).
sharp__allen_cahn_2d is the panel's one genuinely inert dataset: only 46% of its samples moved toward the truth, i.e. its 2.6% displacement is a coin-flip re-roll, not a systematic effect.
ifc_poisson fits its HF target scaler on N_hf = 5 fields, and that turned out NOT to matter; the pedestal/fluctuation geometry (0.1447 / 0.1014) did.

7_gap_and_future.open_question: The scaler bought CALIBRATION, and calibration is exhausted: on ext__helmholtz_2d 91.6% of the gain was per-sample amplitude that an oracle rescale gives for free, and the arm is still 2.2x worse than the constant-field oracle there and 5.77x worse than copy-LF; on ifc_poisson the same G bought a uniform 40% error-energy cut but the model is still 18.5% above the paper bar. The unresolved question is therefore whether the REMAINING error on the two datasets where the scaler acted is an objective problem or an information problem: helmholtz's training loss is still one sample out of 400 (effective N 1.0145, untouched by any global scaler), so is the residual gap the outlier-dominated MSE -- fixable per-sample (RevIN-style target norm, per-sample loss weights, robust loss) -- or is it that an LF-blind conditional generator simply cannot resolve a resonant field, in which case only LF conditioning (s6/s4) helps? Those two have opposite next moves and the round has not separated them.
7_gap_and_future.next_direction: B3 should test the per-sample target normalization the round has now converged on from two directions -- s5-B2's dynamic-range finding (a global scalar cannot de-concentrate the loss; only a PER-SAMPLE scale can) and s2-B2's outlier-domination finding (one train sample = 89-99% of MSE energy) -- as the card's arm A3 `revin_lf` already implemented and ranked but never ran at 200 epochs. Concretely: arm A3 (per-sample s_i = max|LF_i|, both stages, maxabs fallback where the split ships no LF) plus a per-sample-normalized-MSE arm that needs no LF (s_i = max|Y_i| at train time, predicted scale at test time, or an equivalent scale head), on the two datasets where target scaling is a lever at all (ext__helmholtz_2d, ifc_poisson) plus one SCALER_INERT control. Pre-register `G = max|Y_train|/sd(Y_train)` (>= 8) AND a live pattern channel (not LEVEL_ONLY) as the eligibility rule, predict NULLs on the four sharp sets by that rule rather than by |mu|/sd, and instrument the per-batch gradient norm and clip rate so hypothesis H3 (that grad_clip=1.0, not the scaler, is what robustifies the dominant sample) is settled in the same run. The effective-N repair is the thing to measure directly: report effective N of the realized per-batch loss, not of the target energy. MERGE CANDIDATE: this is the same experiment s2_beyond_copy-B3 is heading for from the residual-target side; the two streams should run ONE per-sample-normalization card with a shared arm definition rather than two, with s5 owning the raw-target/LF-blind substrate and s2 owning the residual-target/LF-consuming one.
7_gap_and_future.cross_stream_notes: (1) CORRECTION to the s2_beyond_copy-B2 cross-stream mechanism as applied to global scalers: a GLOBAL target scaler cannot repair effective N. Measured on ext__helmholtz_2d's HF train stage, effective N is 1.0145/400 under maxabs and 1.0179/400 under zscore, and top-1 energy share 0.99284 vs 0.99117 -- a global scalar divides every sample's energy by the same constant, so only the mean can move relative weights. s2-B2's outlier-domination diagnosis is CONFIRMED and in fact stronger than reported (per-sample RMS max/median = 1698 on the raw HF target, not just the residual target), but the fix must be per-sample or objective-side. Any card that proposes a global rescale to fix an outlier-dominated loss is proposing a no-op. (2) NEW STANDING COVARIATE for anyone tuning normalization: use G = max|Y_train|/sd(Y_train), reported as tail (max/rms) x pedestal (rms/sd), NOT |mu|/sd -- the pedestal is absorbed by the output bias. Round-1 panel break: G 6.0 = nothing, G 9.9 = effect. Gate it on tools/dc_pattern_split.py (LEVEL_ONLY datasets are inert under any affine scaler). Tool: tools/target_range_placement_audit.py. (3) FOR s6_local / s4_hybrid_routing: the sharp-2D normalization branch is now closed negatively -- the three LEVEL_ONLY sharp sets sit at 1.04-1.44x their own constant-field oracle under both scalers with demeaned correlation ~0, so what is missing there is a PATTERN-producing mechanism (LF-conditioned, local), consistent with your locality findings. (4) METHOD NOTE for every stream: score movement and function movement are nearly uncorrelated on this panel (ifc_poisson paid from a 3.5% displacement; sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d displaced 42.5% TOWARD the truth and scored flat; sharp__allen_cahn_2d's 2.6% displacement was a coin-flip re-roll at cos -0.013). Before writing 'the knob did nothing', run tools/paired_arm_displacement.py -- 'inert knob' and 'dataset cannot cash it' are different results with different next moves. (5) FOR s7_loss: helmholtz's raw HF target, not just its residual, is outlier-dominated to effective N ~1/400 -- a relative/per-sample loss there is acting on the same pathology this card could not touch.
